newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Taoyuan refinery one month repairs underway.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Taoyuan refinery one month repairs underway.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Monday repair work on its damaged northern Taoyuan refinery had started and would finish within one month.
"Repair works should be completed in less than a month from now," a company official told Reuters.
A fire and explosion on May 29 at Chinese Petroleum's Taoyuan refinery injured one worker and forced the company to reduce its jet fuel production.

The blaze struck the refinery's hydro-desulfurisation units that have a capacity to process 15,000 tonnes of residual oil per month. The refinery's second hydro-desulfurisation unit at the plant can process 30,000 tonnes.
The Taoyuan refinery produces 60,000 tonnes of jet fuel a month at full capacity, mainly supplying the nearby Taipei international airport.
Chinese Petroleum officials said the Taoyuan refinery has been producing jet fuel at about half its capacity since the accident.
